description: Public collection of high-quality templates created by General Legal attorneys with CC0 license
summary: What catches my eye here isn't the legal content (though the CC0 license and the BAA template are genuinely useful for anyone touching health data) but the LLM-optimized markdown format with `<mark>`-tagged fill-in fields. It's a small, well-scoped corpus that makes a concrete agent task—generate a customized privacy policy or DPA for a specific product—actually tractable without the model hallucinating clauses, because the structure tells it exactly which slots to fill and which boilerplate to preserve. For something like Proreerfolio or Oh Tidepool, this is the kind of local-first, composable input that turns "I need to pay a lawyer $2k for a terms-of-use page" into "I need a thirty-minute script against a directory of markdown files," which is the kind of toil removal I actually care about.
